articles.title: Flat-track bullies Celtic continue descent into European irrelevance
articles.summary: BBC Scotland's Tom English reviews another frustrating night in Europe for the Scottish champions.
articles.body:
When Mika Baur scored early in the second half against Celta Vigo, so much in Celtic's garden was rosy.

The team had an intensity now that they didn't have before. They had momentum. Belief. They had a Liam Scales header hopping off the top of the crossbar. The La Liga visitors were under the pump.

It was easy to conclude in those naively optimistic moments that Celta Vigo were all passing and no penetration. They passed it to death and got pretty much nowhere.

More than 350 passes in the opening half and one attempt on target. All very pretty. All very technical. All very tippy-tappy.

The question that Celtic fans will be asking now, some with pitchforks in hand, is what the hell happened in the last half-an-hour of this game. Particularly, what happened from minutes 68 to 71.

From three points to no points. From building on the hiding dished out to Hearts to another loss and getting shunted back to bitterness and rancour.

Celtic suffer third Europa League defeat in row after Celta Vigo turnaround

O'Neill bemoans marginal moments but are Celtic just not good enough?

Latest Celtic news, analysis and fan views

Celtic stopped playing and stopped believing. They were hit with a bit of adversity and they were bowled over by it. Knocked to the ground, never to rise up again.

They'll complain - as they already have - about a foul on Camilo Duran that wasn't picked up just before the equaliser, but there is no talking to the errors they made thereafter.

The inability to deal with a free-kick, the failure to pick up the goalscorer in the first instance and then multiple calamities in the concession of the second goal. How many chances does one side need to get a ball away to safety?

Long before the end, Celtic were gone. Psychologically spent. This is nothing new. Something new would have been the sight of them kicking on at 1-0, but in Europe such strength is a dying art form in this team.

A third straight loss in Europe, 35th out of 36 teams in the Europa League table, only a side from Armenia keeping them off rock bottom. This is their place in the grand scheme now.

Domestic football proves lousy barometer

Chris Sutton calls them flat-track bullies. How many Celtic fans would disagree with that depiction? Not many.

Thursday was yet another example of domestic football being a lousy barometer of Celtic's capacity to win - or even draw - games in Europe.

In the wake of the 7-1 trouncing of Hearts, some Celtic folk with desperately short memories rounded on a few commentators who were critical of Martin O'Neill, his players and this Celtic board following their losses to Rangers and their failures against LASK, Ferencvaros and Benfica.

As if beating up Hearts made it all better. The message, after the goal deluge, was 'what are you saying to it now?' The answer: Exactly as we were saying before.

O'Neill said on Thursday that there are still loads of points to play for - and there are. But it was a claim made from a position of serious weakness. Desperation, almost.

Even at their best in recent decades, Celtic have struggled awfully to win European games on the road. Right now, that looks way beyond them. Winning at home is too much for them these days, too.

So, yes, there are enough points on offer for Celtic to fight their way out of their Europa League dungeon and into the play-off, but in their current state it's more a philosophical thought than an attainable reality.

If you have lost three out of three, have scored three goals and have conceded nine, then banging on about points you might win down the line is an exercise in wishful thinking.

In the here and now, Celtic's standards are plummeting. That's on everybody.

It's on O'Neill and his players, though it's easy to have some sympathy for the manager when he not only has to field questions about the stuff he's responsible for but also come up with answers about stuff that he has no responsibility for - the ongoing circus that is Celtic's relationship with large elements of their own support.

And the blame is also, in greater part, on a board who are happy to have O'Neill and - when he's not around - Shaun Maloney, talking about the disconnect between fans and club, as was the case on Wednesday.

No chief executive, no chairman, no major shareholder and no major shareholder's son are anywhere to be seen when those issues are raised at news conferences. Just a manager or an assistant who, let's face it, have a few other things on their mind.

Do Celtic have vision to make it better?

Just after the television coverage ended on Thursday there was a programme of highlights of big Celtic Park Champions League nights. Remember them?

Celtic beating the Manchester United of Paul Scholes, Ryan Giggs, Cristiano Ronaldo and Wayne Rooney; Celtic beating the AC Milan of Alessandro Nesta, Andrea Pirlo, Clarence Seedorf and Kaka; Celtic beating the Barcelona of Jordi Alba, Xavi, Iniesta and Lionel Messi.

A stadium literally shaking to its very foundations. Packed solid. Deafening. Unforgettable.

Look at it now. Empty seats and people leaving early. A game against the eighth best team in Spain, in a second-tier European competition - defeat and apathy. How they have fallen.

Of course, it might seem a little tiresome looking back at how things were 20 years ago, so let's not. Let's look at how things were in February last year.

Bayern Munich versus Celtic. Ninety-three minutes gone in the second leg in Germany and it's 2-2 on aggregate.

Bayern have started with a front four of Michael Olise, Jamal Musiala, Serge Gnabry and Harry Kane. Thomas Muller has replaced Musiala, Leroy Sane has come on for Gnabry, Kingsley Coman for Kane.

It took Bayern until the fourth minute of added time to see Celtic off. From there to here is some descent into European mediocrity and irrelevance.

O'Neill said that he "can't ask anything more" from his players. He can - and he must.

More must be asked of O'Neill and more - much, much more - must be asked of the board. Bringing in new players and a new manager is easily done, if they so wish. Whether it's the right players and the right manager is a different story, but it can be done in a heartbeat.

Changing a board, and a way of thinking, is a whole lot harder. There's little doubt all of these people want success for Celtic. They might get more of it domestically. They might win another league, another cup, maybe two. That is all highly possible, if not probable.

This question has been asked so many times now - and it's grim that it still has to be asked. What do Celtic stand for? Flat-track bullydom or something more, something more adventurous, something in keeping with the 'great European story' they so often talk about.

Because of the Lisbon Lions it is and always will be the greatest of all Scottish football stories. Nothing is ever likely to surpass it.

But there are other stories, in the present day, that are tiresome for Celtic folk, stories that are playing out now, almost on a loop. From Champions League to Europa League. What's next? Conference League. And after that?

Everyone in power at the club cannot look at that 36-team table and not feel an enormous sense of embarrassment. If they don't, they're really not in the right job.

The question is - do they have any kind of vision to make it better? Many observers of the club might see that as a rhetorical question.

articles.summary: El periodista destacó en La Tribu la importancia del brasileño de cara al duelo ante el Barcelona y criticó la campaña que, a su juicio, existe contra el futbolista madridista

articles.title: Newcastle United: What is going on at 'chaotic' Magpies?
articles.summary: Will the alarm bells be ringing at Newcastle United if they lose to struggling Crystal Palace on Sunday?
articles.body:
Perhaps it was meant to lift spirits after Newcastle 's underwhelming start to the season.

On Tuesday, the Magpies reminded their 2.8 million followers on X that it was 30 years to the day that Kevin Keegan's swashbuckling team of 1996-1997 crushed Manchester United 5-0 at St James' Park to sit top of the Premier League.

It was a flashback to one of the all-time great Newcastle performances, with the social media post , external coming the same week their new German boss Matthias Jaissle is still trying to figure out why his class of 2026-2027 have yet to fire.

Last weekend's home loss to Aston Villa, which was greeted by a chorus of boos from the stands at the final whistle, means Newcastle head into Sunday's game against struggling Crystal Palace at Selhurst Park (14:00 BST) looking to end a run of three defeats in four games.

That sequence includes back-to-back 4-1 away defeats at Leeds United on 14 September and Coventry City on 12 October.

"The pressure will seriously be on if they don't get a result at Palace," Charlotte Robson from the True Faith Newcastle United podcast says.

Supporters have voiced concerns about the team's lack of identity under Jaissle, while questions remain about why, almost 14 months after leaving for Liverpool in a British record £125m deal, Newcastle have struggled to replace Alexander Isak.

"One result can change a lot - all it needs is one good win and all of a sudden you're back on track - but Matthias Jaissle seems very set in his ways at this moment in time," former Newcastle defender John Anderson told BBC Sport.

Chris Sutton, a Premier League winner with Blackburn in 1994-95 - who watched the defeat by Villa at St James' Park for BBC Radio 5 Live - says Newcastle appear "chaotic" under Jaissle.

"There is not enough in the final third in terms of creativity and they have a vulnerability at the back," adds Sutton.

The season is still young but after five years of Eddie Howe, who landed the club's first major domestic trophy since 1955, will the alarm bells be ringing for Jaissle and Newcastle if they lose at Palace?

Alan Shearer predicted it three months ago.

"Speaking purely as a fan, I think we have to get ready for a tough season and some very challenging times ahead," the Newcastle legend told BBC Sport after the long-serving Howe stepped down at the end of July.

Newcastle had already sold England forward Anthony Gordon to Barcelona in a deal worth more than £69m and midfielder Sandro Tonali to Tottenham in a deal worth up to £100m.

"You cannot keep on selling your best players and then hope to be in contention at the top of the table," added Newcastle 's all-time leading goalscorer.

One week after Shearer's words, Bruno Guimaraes joined Arsenal for £75m.

Seven games into the Premier League season, Shearer's gloomy prediction is so far proving correct, with Newcastle on eight points after winning just two top-flight games, away at Tottenham and at home to newly promoted Hull City .

It has been a muddled start with suggestions Newcastle have lacked leadership and experience, with England defender Kieran Trippier, 36, also departing this summer.

"If you had said at the end of last season Newcastle would lose Gordon, Guimaraes, Tonali and Howe, you would probably get this [eight points from seven games]," Rory Smith, football correspondent of the Observer, told BBC Radio 5 Live's The Monday Night Club.

Newcastle spent about £250m on players during the summer transfer window, with many of the new signings aged 21 or under. Two of those players - Ivory coast winger Bazoumana Toure and French midfielder Aladji Bamba - have yet to start a Premier League game despite being available.

Another young recruit, 18-year-old Sean Steur, impressed after starting against Hull in September, but has not played a minute since.

"The profile of the players Newcastle signed in the summer, and it may well bear fruit in time...they went very young and relatively inexperienced," adds Smith.

"They didn't go out and sign a load of established Premier League players."

Newcastle paid Al-Ahli £9.5m in compensation , external to get Jaissle after he had led the Saudi club to consecutive Asian Champions League crowns.

Expectations were high when the former Red Bull Salzburg boss arrived on Tyneside shortly before the start of the season with a strong record of success at his previous clubs in Saudi Arabia and Austria.

Yet Jaissle, 38, is very much unproven in the Premier League.

Seventy-nine days into his reign, it is fair to say the former Red Bull Salzburg boss is still trying to put his own stamp on the team after Howe's long tenure.

Jaissle has issues to solve at both ends of the pitch.

Newcastle are without a home clean sheet in each of their last 16 games in all competitions - the longest run in their history. They are leaking an average of two goals per game in the Premier League - only Crystal Palace (17) and Ipswich (15) have conceded more than Newcastle (14).

Meanwhile, they registered one attempt on target against Villa - their least in a Premier League home match since August 2024. Worryingly, that solo attempt came from defender Sven Botman, while Jaissle used centre-back Dan Burn, a substitute, up front when he was sent on.

There is an argument Newcastle are even yet to adequately replace Callum Wilson. He left the same summer as Isak. Yoane Wissa was technically his replacement with Nick Woltemade the Isak replacement.

Woltemade, who joined in a club-record deal worth up to £69m in August 2025, is now on loan to Juventus, while Wissa has struggled for consistency since returning from injury.

" Newcastle fans have every right to be a little bit concerned," adds Sutton. "They didn't look like scoring against Villa and that is what really concerns Newcastle fans."

Robson believes patience is needed after a summer of upheaval.

There is certainly no panic inside the club right now, with David Hopkinson, the CEO, and Ross Wilson, the sporting director, both applying an air of calm.

It has by no means been a terrible start by Jaissle, who is expected to be given time to get it right. That said, fans want to see an improvement in performances - starting on Sunday.

After the weekend, Newcastle visit Everton in the last-16 of the Carabao Cup next Thursday, host Everton in the Premier League on 2 November and then visit Fulham five days later before the next international break.

Jaissle will not want to go into that without a win in six league and cup games.

"There are more questions being asked now," adds Robson.

"At the start of the season it was made clear in interviews we wanted to be an aggressive attacking team. We are not there yet, we're still working it out."

articles.title: Bruno Fernandes: le roban en su casa y le acusan de "traición" y "sacrilegio" al Manchester United
articles.standfirst: El Manchester United ya maneja los nombres de cinco entrenadores en el caso de que finalmente despidan al técnico Michael Carrick
articles.summary: El Manchester United ya maneja los nombres de cinco entrenadores en el caso de que finalmente despidan al técnico Michael Carrick
articles.body: En Mánchester los dedos acusadores señalan a Bruno Fernandes en la guerra sucia del United, que podría acabar con el despido del entrenador Michael Carrick tras siete partidos sin ganar y sólo dos triunfos en 11 encuentros. El diario 'The Sun' publica que la directiva del Manchester United ya maneja cinco nombres para sustituir a Carrick. En Inglaterra los nombres que se manejan para sustituir a Michael Carrick en el Manchester United son los de Julian Nagelsmann, Fabian Hürzeler, Antonio Conte, Ruud van Nistelrooy y Gareth Southgate. Bruno Fernandes sufrió un robo en su domicilio mientras se encontraba en Italia para jugar en Champions League contra el Como. La BBC informa que la esposa de Fernandes, Ana Pinho, y sus dos hijos pequeños no se encontraban en la lujosa propiedad, valorada en más de 4 millones de euros y situada en Nether Alderley. El 'Daily Mail' publica que los tres intrusos permanecieron en el interior menos de cinco minutos antes de la llegada de la policía, que confirmó que los delincuentes sustrajeron joyas de diseño y otros objetos de gran valor. La Policía fue alertada por un vecino que vio a unos hombres comportándose de manera sospechosa en el jardín trasero. Al parecer, la parte trasera de la casa linda con una zona boscosa; los asaltantes saltaron la valla para entrar, a pesar de que la familia Fernandes contaba con un sistema de cámaras de seguridad y una alarma de alta tecnología. Wayne Rooney, leyenda del Manchester United, calificó a Bruno Fernandes y Lisandro Martínez de "niños egoístas" tras sus críticas hacia Michael Carrick y la directiva del club. "Eso fue solo el principio. Ya lo hemos visto con Bruno, y lo veremos con más jugadores, porque no quieren asumir responsabilidades. Se puede debatir si Bruno tenía razón o no en lo que dijo, pero hay que asumir la responsabilidad sobre el terreno de juego. Hay que asumir la responsabilidad como grupo de jugadores", comentó en el podcast 'United Stand'. El exfutbolista subrayó que "estos jugadores son egoístas. No les importan sus compañeros, ni el entrenador, ni el cuerpo técnico, ni los aficionados; solo les importan ellos mismos. Si no consiguen lo que consideran que merecen, se comportan como niños pequeños: hacen un berrinche y buscan culpar a cualquiera menos a sí mismos". "Si se miran al espejo, Lisandro si Martínez y todos ellos se miran al espejo, verán que quien les devuelve la mirada son ellos mismos, y eso es totalmente insuficiente", apuntó el máximo goleador histórico del United. Wayne Rooney le recomendó a Michael Carrick "salir a luchar; se acabó eso de ser el "chico bueno". Es cierto que hay que hacer ciertas cosas para proteger a los jugadores, pero también hay que salir a defenderse a uno mismo... Porque esos jugadores te van a hundir, y serás tú quien pierda su puesto por su culpa". "Traición", "vergüenza" o "sacrilegio" son algunos de los términos que se leen culpabilizando a Bruno Fernandes, que está en el centro de la polémica después de la derrota del United ante el Como. El exfutbolista Joe Cole fue uno de los más contundentes al considerar en TNT Sports que el capitán del Manchester United cruzó la línea al cuestionar públicamente al entrenador: "Está cuestionando las tácticas. No importa si tiene razón o no. Eso es un sacrilegio". "Ya he jugado con entrenadores cuyas tácticas no me convencían. Puedes comentárselo a un amigo o a tu mujer, pero no puedes presentarte como capitán del club y cuestionar al entrenador. Si vas a hablar, sé directo y hazte responsable de lo que dices. Probablemente él cree que es muy listo, como si estuviera diciendo: 'Podríamos haber hecho esto, pero al final es decisión del entrenador'. Es decir: 'No he dicho exactamente eso, míster'. Pero has dicho lo que has dicho. Consideraste que las tácticas eran erróneas. Puedes ir mañana al despacho del entrenador y decirle: 'Creo que se ha equivocado, míster'. Tener una conversación cara a cara. Como capitán del Manchester United, no puedes salir a la luz pública a cuestionar las tácticas. Bruno ha actuado muy mal. Esto nunca habría ocurrido con Sir Alex Ferguson", apuntó. Kasper Schmeichel, exportero e hijo de Peter Schmeichel, también criticó en la BBC a Bruno Fernandes: "Teniendo en cuenta lo que ocurrió la semana pasada (la declaraciones de Lisandro Martínez) y todo lo que ha pasado, probablemente no debería decir estas cosas, porque solo va a agravar los problemas. Con la experiencia, aprendemos que estos asuntos deben quedarse dentro del club. Es un problema. Michael Carrick no necesitaba esto, el club no necesitaba esto. Se están exponiendo todos los problemas del Manchester United". El exfutbolista Stephen Warnock subrayó, sobre las declaraciones de Bruno Fernandes, "te guste o no el entrenador, tienes que unirte al resto y decir: '¿Cómo arreglamos esto?'. Los jugadores con más experiencia deben hablar con el entrenador, decirle que no están de acuerdo con las tácticas, que consideran que el equipo no planteó bien el partido, y preguntarle cómo pueden seguir adelante. Cuando empiezas a hablar de estas cosas en público, no acaba bien para nadie», explicó. Frank Leboeuf fue un poco más contundente en la cadena ESPN sobre Bruno Fernandes: "Estamos ante una traición. Una traición al entrenador, a los aficionados y al club por parte de los jugadores. odemos hablar de las tácticas; tal vez no hayan sido las mejores. Pero quizás Michael Carrick conozca demasiado bien a los jugadores y sepa de qué son incapaces. Tal vez por eso haya sido un poco más defensivo. Están dejando quedar mal al entrenador. No corren por él, no corren por el club, no dan el 100 %". Gabriel Agbonlahor, exdelantero del Aston Villa, cuestionó la capacidad de Bruno Fernandes para ejercer el rol de capitán en el Manchester United: "Es una vergüenza. Ha hundido al entrenador. Llevo años diciendo esto: ahora, cuando las cosas se ponen difíciles en el Manchester United, está demostrando quién es. ¿Cómo puede ser el capitán de ese club?... Fue una vergüenza. Se pasaba todo el tiempo perdiendo el balón y levantando los brazos".

articles.title: Gianni Infantino: Asian football chief gives Fifa president re-election lift
articles.summary: Gianni Infantino's hopes of being re-elected Fifa president are enhanced by an endorsement from the Asian Football Confederation.
articles.body:
Gianni Infantino's hopes of being re-elected Fifa president have been given a major boost by an endorsement from the head of the Asian Football Confederation.

President Sheikh Salman bin Ibrahim Al Khalifa Salman told the confederation's Congress in Tokyo - which was attended by Infantino - that "we reaffirm our full commitment, of course, to supporting you as you seek a new mandate as president".

Sheikh Salman's support represents a significant u-turn just two months after he signed a joint letter with the heads of Uefa and Concacaf criticising Infantino over his failed plan to sell stakes in the World Cup to private investors.

At the time the three confederations accused him of breaking trust "through deception" over the Fifa Forward Enterprise scheme.

But Sheikh Salman told the meeting in Japan it was time "to move forward".

"I've spoken to a lot of members within this continent. I know your feeling and I think your commitment is clear as well. Your support to Gianni is very clear," he added.

"Yes, we had some issues, we spoke about them in the past, but let's not relate the two things together...

"As one Asian family, we are ready to move forward, united in your support, Gianni."

Alongside Infantino's power base in Africa and South America, Sheikh Salman's endorsement could be crucial in ensuring the Fifa president secures a fourth and final term.

At the election in Rabat in March, Uefa will have 55 votes, Africa 54, Asia 46, Concacaf 35, Oceania 11 and Conmebol 10.

The deadline for candidates to confirm they are standing against Infantino is 18 November - although none have yet filed and he could stand unopposed. Potential rivals like Victor Montagliani, the president of Concacaf, and Uefa chief Aleksander Ceferin have let it be known they are not contenders, while Infantino has been touring the world, shoring up his position.

At a meeting of Fifa's Council last week, Infantino apologised for his World Cup sell-off plan , but failed to offer a full explanation for how the proposal was devised.

He also proposed to increase the amount of money handed out for football development across the world by $3.4bn (£2.6bn).

Uefa has since told Fifa it must release key documents and answer all questions relating to its governance and decision-making by 2 November.

articles.title: Raúl Varela analiza el Clásico: "Huele a empate bueno para los dos"
articles.standfirst: El periodista reflexiona en La Tribu sobre el cambio de sensaciones tras la jornada europea, las dudas del Real Madrid, las certezas del Barça y el ruido arbitral que rodea al partido
articles.summary: El periodista reflexiona en La Tribu sobre el cambio de sensaciones tras la jornada europea, las dudas del Real Madrid, las certezas del Barça y el ruido arbitral que rodea al partido
articles.body: El primer Clásico de la temporada llega con un escenario diferente al que se dibujaba hace apenas unos días. Así lo considera Raúl Varela, que en su opinión en La Tribu pone el foco en el cambio de perspectiva que ha dejado la semana europea y en las dudas que todavía rodean al Real Madrid, pese a los últimos movimientos de José Mourinho. "Lo que parecía un Barça inabordable se ha convertido en un 'sí, pero…' de manual", escribe Varela, que también apunta a un cambio en la percepción sobre el conjunto blanco: "Los que ya daban por enterrado y finiquitado el proyecto de Mou como entrenador del Madrid ya admiten que salir vivos del Camp Nou es probable". Para Varela, la principal diferencia entre ambos equipos está en el momento de construcción futbolística. El Barcelona de Hansi Flick llega con una estructura más asentada, mientras que el Real Madrid continúa descubriendo alternativas y ajustando piezas. "Lo cierto es que ahora mismo hay muchas más certezas en este Barça donde Flick lo tiene todo más rodado y solo debe improvisar una línea defensiva", explica el periodista, que recuerda las dificultades provocadas por las lesiones en esa zona. La situación madridista es muy distinta. Varela describe el proceso de cambios del equipo blanco con una imagen muy gráfica: "Parece un yacimiento arqueológico en el que pasando la brocha van apareciendo pequeños tesoros". En ese escenario, destaca el nuevo papel de Fede Valverde en el lateral derecho y la posibilidad de que Eduardo Camavinga gane protagonismo en el centro del campo. También menciona a Diomandé como una alternativa que podría resultar importante ante el Barcelona. Otro de los aspectos que analiza Varela es la ausencia de Vinicius. En su opinión, la baja del brasileño no tiene por qué favorecer al Barcelona en todos los sentidos, ya que su perfil también aporta un componente emocional al encuentro. "El hecho de que ese matiz provocador del extremo brasileño se quede en su chalet de la capital de España, le quita también un poco de punch ambiental al choque", apunta. El periodista también dedica parte de su reflexión a la polémica arbitral que ha acompañado la previa. "Se ha abierto un casting para designar un trencilla que difícilmente pasará desapercibido como siempre fue su deseo", escribe Varela, en referencia al ruido generado alrededor de la designación arbitral. La previa llega cargada de nombres propios y posibles consecuencias deportivas. Lamine Yamal, Mbappé, Courtois, Joan, Rodri y Bellingham aparecen en el análisis de Varela, junto a dos escenarios que pueden marcar el relato posterior: la posibilidad de que el Madrid se quede a nueve puntos o que el Barcelona encadene dos derrotas consecutivas. El periodista concluye su reflexión sin señalar un favorito definitivo y con una idea clara sobre el resultado que podría dejar el encuentro: "Huele a empate bueno para los dos". Una posibilidad que, en medio de las dudas, las expectativas y el ruido de la previa, permitiría aplazar algunas de las conclusiones que rodean a ambos equipos.

articles.title: FPL gameweek eight tips: Bring Erling Haaland back as captain?
articles.summary: BBC Sport FPL expert Holly Shand looks at some of the biggest dilemmas facing FPL managers heading into gameweek eight.
articles.body:
BBC Sport FPL expert Holly Shand looks at some of the biggest dilemmas facing FPL managers heading into gameweek eight.

Enzo Maresca confirmed on Tuesday night that Erling Haaland (£13.7m) is fit to start against Aston Villa on Saturday, having been an unused substitute in Manchester City 's 5-1 Champions League win against AEK Athens.

That immediately puts him at the top of the captaincy contenders this weekend. He has eight goals from seven league games this season, but has not scored in his past four Premier League appearance against Aston Villa .

Chelsea attackers headline the list of alternative options, with Joao Pedro (£7.9m) their best fantasy asset to date, with five goals and three assists. Cole Palmer (£9.7m) has the higher ceiling, though, given that he takes penalties.

Best midfield replacements for Saka, Semenyo and Szoboszlai?

Arsenal 's Bukayo Saka (£9.6m) picked up a quadricps injury in the Champions League on Wednesday night, to add to the injury woes of our template fantasy midfielders, with Liverpool 's Dominik Szoboszlai (£6.8m) and City's Antoine Semenyo (£8.3m) already ruled out long term.

There is plenty of interest in City's midfield, with a hope that rotation will be eased with Semenyo ruled out.

Rayan Cherki (£8m) is seeing the most transfer traffic, but it was Phil Foden (£6.8m) who shone with a hat-trick in midweek. Jeremy Doku (£7.5m) has three goal involvements in three games.

Is it still worth investing in Brighton?

Absolutely. Three of the top five players in the game are Brighton assets. Out-of-position defender Maxim de Cuyper (£5.3m) leads the way, with Pascal Gross (£6.2m) one point behind him - level with Haaland - and centre-back Luka Vuskovic (£5.1m) in fourth.

Add into the mix Bart Verbruggen (£4.6m) among the top three goalkeepers and Charalampos Kostoulas (£5.7m) in the top three strikers.

They are showing all the hallmarks of being season keepers, with the Seagulls scoring a league-leading 23 goals and conceding a league-lowest of five.

Should you start Gross and De Cuyper at Anfield?

Yes. I know it is deceiving seeing De Cuyper listed as a defender, but he is effectively a £5.1m attacking winger who is also eligible for clean sheet points. He is the highest-scoring asset in the game, with five goal involvements in seven games, the most of any defender. Consider him fixture-proof.

Gross is another player difficult to bench, especially when you consider he is on penalties. No other player can match his nine goal involvements, and he ranks second for key passes (19) and big chances created (six).

Liverpool have yet to win at home in the league this season, scoring two goals and conceding five.

Who are the best DefCon defenders to target?

Vuskovic has to be at the top of the list for defensive contribution points - or 'DefCons', with Brighton keeping a leading five clean sheets in seven games this season.

He has secured the two-point defensive contribution bonus in four of those games, while also notching two goal involvements, with a leading four big chances among defenders.

Leeds United 's Tarik Muharemovic (£5m) is also on the list, hitting DefCons on four occasions. He got his second assist of the season last time out, having had six shots in the box.

Coventry City 's Bobby Thomas (£4m) leads the way with 84 defensive contributions and has had 10 shots in the penalty area.

City's Josko Gvardiol produced one goal, two clean sheets and three assists in his opening five games, but has frustrated his owners by being benched against Liverpool and Ipswich Town in gameweek six and seven.

However, with reports that Nico O'Reilly is struggling with a back problem, Gvardiol could be set for a run of games. With this in mind, I would keep hold of him unless you are sitting on a stack of transfers and have no other issues in your team.

articles.title: Man City Sanctions: Would Arsenal Fans Be Happy With Relegation?
articles.summary: Something tells me in the next few months we are going to get many theories from journalists regarding Man City’s future.Since growing up, my favourite footb...
articles.body:
Something tells me in the next few months we are going to get many theories from journalists regarding Man City's future.

Since growing up, my favourite football writer has always been Oliver Holt and (now working for the Daily Mail) he claims sources close to the independent commission case are telling him that a realistic sanction for being guilty of 114 charges for financial breaches could essentially be two points deductions that would effectively guarantee relegation to the Championship and make an immediate return unlikely.

The EFL is a separate company to the Premier League, so doesn't have to be dictated to, although it does have its own rules which state it can impose its own points deductions on any club relegated to it because of disciplinary sanctions.

This would be the only way to appease the anger of the rest of the football pyramid, who understandably fear the Sky Blues on 0 points would have the resources to take away a promotion spot worth 200 million.

That's deemed the most realistic way to properly hurt the Citizens on and off the pitch where it makes an impact.

Would Relegation Really Hurt Manchester City?

On the same wages, the majority of the dressing room would be convinced to spend a year in the English second tier if they knew it was for only 12 months and then they go back to challenging for the Premiership.

Their fans have already made it clear they would embrace the change with defiance and humour, but would their smiles be removed if a punishment put them bottom of the Prem, which led to being bottom of the second tier, making promotion at the first try unrealistic?

That would mean no top-flight fixtures at the Etihad until at least the 2028-2029 season, which would then mean the earliest the stadium hosts the Champions League would be the 2029-2030 campaign.

That's a long time for the likes of Haaland to have his career on hold.

Yet would that be enough to appease Gooners?

In the short term, it removes an obstacle in Arsenal's bid to lift more Premierships, but long term I know peers who want more.

There isn't a sanction that's going to please everyone, but as Mr Holt also explains, those who want Man City expelled from the top flight and starting again at the bottom of the football pyramid might be disappointed.

Haaland v Eze (Photo by Justin Setterfield/Getty Images)

Should Manchester City Be Given a Way Back?

As a brand, it's hard for England to promote their league as the best in the world if they are erasing their eight-time champions from existence, and also would it be fair for an institution 146 years old to be ruined by the acts of one regime?

So whatever consequences they face, Man City need the chance to breathe again.

If you give them nothing, then they equally have nothing to lose.

If you want them to take their medicine, don't give any lawyers reason to argue that a sanction is not proportionate.

So Gooners, would you be happy with a points deduction and relegation as Oliver Holt is suggesting, or do you want more blood?

Would two points deductions and potentially years outside the Premier League be punishment enough for Manchester City, or would anything short of expulsion fail to deliver justice? articles.title: Real Sociedad equal their record European away win at Lillestrøm as Sergio Gómez becomes their top Europa League scorer
articles.summary: Real Sociedad won 6-0 in Norway to claim their first Europa League league-phase victory of the season, matching the biggest away win in their European histor...
articles.body:
Real Sociedad won 6-0 in Norway to claim their first Europa League league-phase victory of the season, matching the biggest away win in their European history. Left-back Sergio Gómez scored twice and is now the club's top scorer in the competition ahead of Lyon's visit to Anoeta.

The scoreline at Åråsen Stadion equalled the biggest away win in the club's European history, according to Noticias de Gipuzkoa. The mark dates from a 6-0 win at Vardar on matchday three in 2017. UEFA described that game at the time as the biggest away win in Europa League history.

Matarazzo's side had struggled before Thursday. They lost 2-1 at home to Bournemouth on matchday one. They then drew 1-1 away to Union SG on matchday two.

Oyarzabal's eight-minute spell settled the game early

Lillestrøm had the better of the opening minutes and pressed the visitors hard. Within eight minutes, Oyarzabal's creativity then turned the match. Sergio Gómez struck in the 25th and 27th minutes. The first came with his left foot, the second with a delicate right-footed finish past Dahlberg. Luka Sučić added the third in the 33rd minute.

The hosts had a chance to respond after the break. Thomas Lehne Olsen missed a penalty in the 50th minute. Orri Steinn Óskarsson made it four in the 64th minute from a Gonçalo Guedes assist. Sučić scored again in the 72nd. Arsen Zakharyan completed the rout in the 80th minute from Benat Turrientes's pass.

The figures point to a closer contest than the score. Expected goals finished 2.29 for Lillestrøm against 2.46 for Real Sociedad. The hosts had 14 shots to 16. The gap lay in accuracy: Real Sociedad put 8 shots on target, Lillestrøm 2. The visitors also had 56% of possession.

For Lillestrøm, the defeat compounds a difficult start. They had lost 2-1 at home to Torreense and drawn 1-1 at Sparta Praha in their first two league-phase games.

A left-back is now Real Sociedad's top scorer in Europe

No Real Sociedad player has scored more in this season's competition than Sergio Gómez, whose opening European goal came in the defeat to Bournemouth. The data provider rated him 9.04, just ahead of Sučić on 9.02.

Spain's other Europa League side also won away on matchday three. Celta came from behind to beat Celtic 2-1 in Glasgow. Javi Rodríguez scored both of their goals.

Real Sociedad return to LaLiga against Levante at Anoeta on Sunday 25 October. That matchday 10 fixture kicks off at 17:30. Later European dates include a trip to Crystal Palace at Selhurst Park on 26 November. Torreense come to San Sebastián on 10 December. The league phase ends away to Juventus on 28 January 2027.

articles.title: Here’s why Leipzig fans booed Real Madrid defender at the Bernabeu despite never facing him before
articles.summary: Marc Cucurella was greeted with a standing ovation from Real Madrid supporters but also with a chorus of boos from RB Leipzig fans when he came on during the...
articles.body:
Marc Cucurella was greeted with a standing ovation from Real Madrid supporters but also with a chorus of boos from RB Leipzig fans when he came on during the 4-1 victory over the German side .

The reaction appeared puzzling because the Spanish defender had never faced Leipzig before, but the hostility can be traced back to Spain's controversial Euro 2024 quarter-final against Germany.

Notably, Cucurella replaced Carreras in the 70th minute, drawing applause from the home crowd at the Bernabeu.

Leipzig's travelling supporters, however, responded differently, reviving memories of an incident that remains contentious among German football fans.

Cucurella's Euro 2024 handball incident explains the boos

The hostility dates back to the European Championship quarter-final between Spain and Germany, played on German soil in 2024.

Spain won 2-1 to reach the semi-finals, but one incident involving Cucurella became a major talking point.

During the match, Germany appealed for a penalty after a shot from Toni Kroos struck Cucurella's arm inside the penalty area.

The referee did not award a spot-kick, leaving German players and supporters frustrated with the decision.

The incident became one of the defining controversies of Spain's run through the tournament.

Marc Cucurella was booed by the Leipzig fans. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images)

Although Spain ultimately went on to win the European Championship, the disputed penalty appeal remained a source of anger among some German supporters.

Leipzig supporters revive Germany's frustration at the Bernabeu

Cucurella's appearance against Leipzig offered a reminder that the controversy had not been forgotten by everyone.

The boos from the away section suggested that some German fans still associate the defender with the quarter-final decision, despite his having no previous history against the Bundesliga club.

The reaction at the Bernabeu therefore had little to do with the Real Madrid-Leipzig contest itself. Instead, it showed lingering frustration from an international match played more than two years earlier.

articles.title: Rival watch: Jose Mourinho’s El Clasico plan reveals how Real Madrid intend to face Barcelona
articles.summary: Real Madrid coach Jose Mourinho is preparing to make several tactical decisions for Sunday’s El Clasico against Barcelona.Los Blancos come into this game hop...
articles.body:
Real Madrid coach Jose Mourinho is preparing to make several tactical decisions for Sunday's El Clasico against Barcelona.

Los Blancos come into this game hoping to close the six-point gap that Hansi Flick's Barça have established at the top of the table.

According to MARCA , Federico Valverde, Arda Guler and Yan Diomande are expected to occupy important roles in Madrid's starting XI.

Mourinho's plan involves deploying Valverde at right-back, Guler on the right wing and Diomande on the left, while Aurelien Tchouameni and Eduardo Camavinga form a double pivot in midfield.

Mourinho plans a different midfield and attacking structure

Valverde's expected inclusion at right-back would continue a tactical adjustment that has recently helped Madrid improve their possession game.

The Uruguayan offers energy, defensive recovery and the ability to move into midfield when Madrid build attacks.

Arda Guler is expected to start on the right wing against Barcelona. (Photo by Denis Doyle/Getty Images)

Ahead of him, Guler would provide creativity from the right flank, using his left foot to drift inside and connect with Madrid's central players.

Meanwhile, Tchouameni and Camavinga would give Mourinho a physically strong midfield partnership capable of protecting the defence and competing for second balls.

Diomande's proposed role on the opposite wing would add pace and directness, and he will look to target Xavi Espart, who is likely to start at right-back for Barça .

What Mourinho's plan means for Barcelona

For Hansi Flick, the reported set-up offers several tactical clues ahead of Sunday's encounter.

Guler's tendency to move inside could create combinations with Valverde, making Barcelona's left-sided defensive organisation particularly important.

However, that movement could also leave space behind Valverde when Madrid commit players forward.

Barcelona's attackers must be prepared to exploit those situations quickly rather than allowing Madrid to recover their defensive shape.

Tchouameni and Camavinga could start together in midfield for El Clasico. (Photo by Giuseppe CACACE / AFP) (Photo by GIUSEPPE CACACE/AFP via Getty Images)

The Tchouameni-Camavinga partnership presents another challenge. Their physicality could make central progression difficult.

Barça 's midfield is the best there is in world football, and they will have to use their technical prowess to beat Madrid's physicality.

Madrid have looked better in these last two games since Jose Mourinho made these tactical adjustments, and Barça need to be wary of those changes.

However, playing at the Camp Nou , Flick's side should determine how the game is played, and it remains to be seen how Barça set up against Madrid.

articles.title: Hull City vs Brentford Match Preview: Team News, TV & Prediction
articles.summary: Brentford travel to Hull City on Sunday looking to bounce back from their Liverpool defeat. Latest team news, kick-off details, TV coverage and prediction.
articles.body:
Brentford travel to Hull City on Sunday looking to put their first defeat of the season behind them, although Keith Andrews will have to make changes to his midfield following last weekend's 2-1 loss to Liverpool.

The Bees had been unbeaten in their opening six Premier League matches before Liverpool's visit to the Gtech Community Stadium, where Keane Lewis-Potter's first-half opener was eventually overturned after Yehor Yarmoliuk received a straight red card.

Vitaly Janelt was also dismissed late on, leaving Andrews without two regular midfield options for the trip to the MKM Stadium.

Hull have made an encouraging return to the Premier League after nine years away, collecting nine points from seven matches. They sit just one point behind sixth-placed Brentford , having already beaten Manchester United and Newcastle United and drawn with Chelsea, Aston Villa and Everton.

However, the Tigers were beaten 1-0 by Fulham last weekend, with manager Sergej Jakirović particularly unhappy with his team's performance.

Keith Andrews has confirmed that Jannik Schuster is available for Sunday's trip to Hull City after recovering from a knock and illness, with no fresh injuries or setbacks reported ahead of the game.

Though, the Bees head coach will be without Yehor Yarmoliuk and Vitaly Janelt after their dismissals against Liverpool. Both midfielders are suspended, leaving Andrews with decisions to make in an area of the pitch that has been relatively settled this season.

Mamadou Sangaré could be handed an opportunity from the start, having impressed after coming off the bench against Liverpool. Mathias Jensen and Mikkel Damsgaard provide further options as Andrews considers how best to compensate for the two absences.

Schuster's return is a welcome boost, particularly after Brentford 's recent defensive injury concerns. Nathan Collins and Sepp van den Berg have also been working their way back to full fitness, with the latter returning to the starting XI against Liverpool.

Josh Dasilva, Antoni Milambo and Kaye Furo remain among Brentford's longer-term absentees.

Keane Lewis-Potter is another player likely to feature against his former club, having scored Brentford's opening goal against Liverpool last weekend.

Hull's return to the top flight has gone better than many expected, particularly at home.

Jakirović's side have conceded just twice at the MKM Stadium this season, despite regularly allowing opponents to dominate possession. Their opening-day victory over Manchester United was followed by a goalless draw against Aston Villa and another point against Everton.

Last weekend's performance at Fulham was considerably less encouraging, with Alex Iwobi scoring the only goal.

"We were very, very poor," Jakirović admitted afterwards, before suggesting changes could be needed.

Hull also have their own injury concerns. Robinio Vaz suffered an Achilles problem against Fulham, while Jack Butland, Matt Targett, Charlie Hughes, Eliot Matazo, Darko Gyabi and Ilyas Ansah have been among those unavailable.

Mohamed-Ali Cho and Lucas Gourna-Douath are also dealing with fitness problems.

Mohamed Belloumi has been one of Hull's standout attacking players, scoring three Premier League goals and threatening from the right.

What to Expect From Hull City vs Brentford

Brentford could have more possession than usual on Sunday.

Hull have averaged just 32 per cent possession in their opening seven Premier League matches, preferring to defend in numbers and attack quickly when opportunities arise.

They have been particularly difficult to break down at home, and Andrews will need his midfield to create openings against a side comfortable playing without the ball.

Damsgaard and Jensen could play an important role, although the absence of Janelt and Yarmoliuk leaves Brentford with less of their usual midfield protection.

Hull are dangerous when they win possession high up the pitch, having already scored three goals from high turnovers this season. Belloumi's pace and willingness to take on defenders will also give Brentford something to consider.

The clubs have a history, although Sunday's fixture will be their first meeting in the Premier League.

The Bees won 5-1 on their last visit to Hull in February 2020, with Saïd Benrahma scoring a hat-trick. Lewis-Potter was in the Hull side that afternoon.

Hull City host Brentford at the MKM Stadium on Sunday, October 25, 2026, with kick-off scheduled for 2pm GMT.

The UK clocks go back on Sunday morning so the match will take place after the change from British Summer Time.

Sky Sports will broadcast the match live in the United Kingdom, with coverage on Sky Sports

Supporters in the United States can watch live on Peacock, with kick-off at 10am ET, 9am CT, 8am MT and 7am PT.

Canadian viewers can follow the match on Fubo, while Australian viewers can watch on Stan Sport.

Brentford have responded well to difficult situations under Andrews, but losing two midfielders to suspension is far from ideal against a Hull side that have proved difficult to beat at home.

The Tigers have shown they can compete with more established Premier League opposition, and their defensive organisation could make chances difficult to come by.

Brentford have enough quality to take something from the trip, although a tight contest looks likely.

articles.title: Doubt Over Matias Fernandez-Pardo As No Sight At Training After Being Ill
articles.summary: A reported training absence has sparked selection concerns for the €60 million Belgian forward, as Matthias Jaissle weighs his attacking options ahead of a c...
articles.body:
Newcastle United have been handed a potential concern over Matias Fernandez-Pardo after the forward was reportedly absent from training following a recent illness, leaving questions over his availability for the club's upcoming fixture.

The Belgian attacker, who arrived at St James' Park from Lille in a reported €60 million deal, has been attracting attention as Newcastle continue to develop their attacking options under head coach Matthias Jaissle. However, his absence from training has raised uncertainty over whether he will be available for selection.

At this stage, there is no confirmed indication that Fernandez-Pardo is dealing with a serious injury. Instead, the reported illness appears to be the immediate concern, although the full extent of the situation and its impact on his preparations remain unclear.

For Newcastle, the priority will be ensuring the forward has recovered sufficiently before making any decision regarding his involvement.

Fernandez-Pardo's Availability In Question

Missing a training session does not automatically mean a player will be unavailable for a match, particularly when illness is involved. Recovery times can vary, and players may return to the training ground once they are feeling better and able to resume their normal workload.

Nevertheless, the timing of Fernandez-Pardo's absence could prove significant if Newcastle are preparing for an important Premier League encounter.

Jaissle's approach places considerable emphasis on intensity, aggressive pressing and quick transitions. Those demands require players to be physically prepared, making it important that any returning player is fully recovered before being considered for selection.

If Fernandez-Pardo has been struggling with illness over recent days, Newcastle's medical staff will need to assess his condition before determining whether he can participate in full training.

The club will also be keen to avoid rushing him back prematurely, particularly if there is any risk that doing so could prolong his recovery.

An Important Player For Newcastle's Attacking Plans

Fernandez-Pardo's arrival from Lille was viewed as a significant investment in Newcastle's attacking future. His technical ability, movement and versatility offer the potential to provide Jaissle with additional options across the forward line.

The Belgian youngster's ability to operate in different attacking positions could prove particularly valuable as Newcastle look to establish greater consistency in their performances.

Competition for places remains important, and any absence could provide an opportunity for another member of the squad to step into the starting line-up or make an impression from the bench.

However, Newcastle will naturally hope Fernandez-Pardo is available as soon as possible, especially if he has been building momentum in training and working towards a more prominent role within the team.

With a demanding schedule requiring careful management of the squad, maintaining the availability of attacking players will be an important consideration for Jaissle and his coaching staff.

For now, uncertainty remains over Fernandez-Pardo's immediate availability following his reported illness and absence from training.

A return to the training ground would provide an encouraging indication that the forward is recovering, although his fitness would still need to be assessed before any decision is made about matchday involvement.

Supporters will be hoping the situation proves to be a short-term issue rather than something that keeps the attacker sidelined for an extended period.

Until further information becomes available from Newcastle United or the head coach, it would be premature to conclude that Fernandez-Pardo will definitely miss the next fixture.

The key question is whether he can recover in time to rejoin the squad and be considered for selection.

Newcastle will be hoping for positive news on Fernandez-Pardo's condition, with his availability potentially providing Jaissle with another valuable attacking option in the coming days.

articles.title: Can Jeremy Doku hit the heights of Vinicius Jr & Luis Diaz? Man City star told where he needs to improve in order to join the global elite of left wingers
articles.summary: Philippe Albert has told GOAL that Manchester City star Jeremy Doku is capable of hitting the heights scaled by fellow left wingers Vinicius Junior and Luis...
articles.body:
Doku's game is all about running at opposition full-backs and forcing them onto the back foot. His pace allows direct bursts into the final third to be made, while his technical ability means that defenders can be left tied up in knots .

Those qualities were first showcased when making a senior breakthrough in his homeland with Anderlecht. It was never going to take long for such potential to be noted, with Rennes being the ones to take him to France in 2020.

Three seasons there saw his output in the goal contributions department continue to rise, with leading sides from across Europe paying close attention to a talented playmaker with a low centre of gravity.

City ultimately won the race for a much sought-after signature, with the Premier League heavyweights parting with a £55 million ($74m) transfer fee. Doku had to prove his worth to demanding Catalan coach Pep Guardiola.

He was not always a guaranteed starter during the early part of his time in England, but a more regular role was eventually nailed down . Premier League, FA Cup, Carabao Cup, Community Shield and FIFA Club World Cup triumphs have been savoured with the Blues.

Can Doku emulate output of Vini Jr & Diaz?

There is the promise of even more to come from Doku, with the general consensus being that he can become more prolific on the goal front - having never previously broken into double figures across a single campaign.

Those are the kind of numbers that he needs to be posting in order to rub shoulders with the likes of Real Madrid 'Galactico' Vinicius and Bayern Munich superstar Diaz at the very top of the world game - with two South American forwards often registering 20-plus goals alongside impressive tallies of assists.

Asked if Doku can reach that level , ex-Belgium international Albert - who was speaking in association with Haypp - told GOAL : "Of course. Doku has plenty of qualities.

"I saw him when he started here in Belgium with Anderlecht, and as soon as he touched the ball, as soon as he played, everybody in Belgium knew that he would become a terrific player.

"The problem is Jeremy is still young and sometimes he makes great things, but sometimes he touches the ball too much. With Guardiola, he went to another level.

"In the World Cup, he was very unlucky with Belgium because he had to come back for the birth of his child and he didn't play a very good World Cup. Since then, one or two players came into the national team and Jeremy will have some difficulties to get back in the starting XI with Belgium.

"But if he plays with Man City and is in good shape, he will always be on the team sheet."

Belgian believes he can be one of the best

Doku believes that he can become one of the best around, telling The Guardian in April of his efforts to emulate Vini and Co: "I feel like if I have goals we are talking about a different conversation. Assists - I'm fine.

"I have to be more in the areas where you can score easy goals, tap-ins. When I look at my goals, every time they are with dribbles. I want to score even five tap-ins a-season – that would make a big difference.

"A winger needs to score. If I have those goals then I believe that I can get there to be the world's best winger, for sure, 100%."

Doku's ambition is to be admired , and every player should always be striving for continuous improvement. The odd distraction has, however, crept in at City - with 114 Financial Fair Player (FFP) charges and the threat of serious punishments hanging over the Etihad Stadium .

It has been suggested that City could be stung with a points deduction that leads to them being relegated into the Championship. Doku will not want to be playing second tier football at this stage of his career, with potential transfer destinations for 2027 already being speculated on.

articles.title: El top 8 se pone a sólo tres puntos
articles.standfirst: La Real, gracias a su goleada en Lillestrom y a las derrotas de algunos rivales, se coloca decimocuarta en una clasificación que ve con más optimismo
articles.summary: La Real, gracias a su goleada en Lillestrom y a las derrotas de algunos rivales, se coloca decimocuarta en una clasificación que ve con más optimismo
articles.body: La Real Sociedad ha sido uno de los equipos que más beneficio han sacado a la tercera jornada de la fase Liga de esta Europa League, ya que a su gran victoria por 0-6 en Lillestrom vio como se sumaban los tropiezos de unos cuantos de los rivales que tenía por delante, entre ellos Juventus, Besiktas o Lyon, su próximo rival, lo que ha hecho que con los cuatro puntos que suma se haya situado decimocuarta en la clasificación, a sólo tres de distancia del top 8. La Real ha ascendido ocho puestos en esta jornada, al pasar del vigesimosegundo a ese decimocuarto que hemos dicho, superando a Milan, Torreense u Ofi Creta, y se ha situado en el grupo de hasta ocho equipos con cuatro puntos, siendo el primero de todos ellos en la tabla, gracias a esa goleada por 0-6. Desde su posición, el conjunto de Matarazzo ve ahora como el top 8 se ha acercado de seis a sólo tres puntos, ya que algunos de los que habían hecho pleno en las dos primeras jornadas no consiguieron su tercer triunfo, como la Juventus, el Besiktas o el Lyon, su próximo rival, el 5 de noviembre en Anoeta. Los turcos y los italianos, junto a una sorprendente Union Saint Gilloise, son los que cierran ahora mismo el top 8, con siete puntos, una cifra a la que la Real llegaría de vencer a los franceses, a los que pasaría, ya que están con seis. El resto de los rivales que quedan están así a día de hoy: Crystal Palace (15º con cuatro puntos), Torreense (28º con tres), Viktoria Plzen (33º con cero) y Juventus (7ª con siete). Por delante, se mantienen intratables Benfica, Bayer Leverkusen, Bournemouth, Ferencváros y el Olympiacos de Imanol Alguacil, únicos cinco clubes que han hecho nueve de nueve. Los ingleses se llevaron los tres en juego en San Sebastián por una muy mala primera parte txuriurdin, y los otros cuatro no están en el calendario, por lo que tras ganar en Noruega se puede mirar con bastante más optimismo el futuro en esta competición.

articles.title: How three men and one win can help Tottenham shake off ‘Spursy’ tag
articles.summary: The mantra of being ‘Spursy’ has long been a source of irritation for Tottenham Hotspur fans – largely because it originates in a reality the club has been t...
articles.body:
The mantra of being 'Spursy' has long been a source of irritation for Tottenham Hotspur fans – largely because it originates in a reality the club has been trying to shake.

Relinquishing leads, wilting under pressure and a lack of collective belief has led to Spurs spending years trying to escape the label.

Changing that reputation will take more than a new manager, a few impressive performances or promises of a brighter future.

It requires a change in mentality — and there are hopes Roberto De Zerbi, alongside the grit of players such as Dejan Kulusevski and James Maddison, could help Spurs begin that process.

De Zerbi has a clearly defined footballing philosophy, built around bravery in possession, intelligent movement and the willingness to take risks.

His teams are expected to play with conviction rather than simply react to their opponents. It's also painstakingly evident how much of passionate character he is and how unrelenting he is in relation to his methods.

If De Zerbi can forge a sense of togetherness and belief in the current, supremely gifted playing squad, Tottenham are capable of creating a special time akin to the years under Mauricio Pochettino.

However, the difference between a talented team and a successful one is often what happens when everything is going against it.

Grit must become part of Tottenham's identity

Dejan Kulusevski and James Maddison's importance to Tottenham cannot be understated and the duo offer an example of the character Tottenham need. Both bring personality and competitive edge, and neither is short of confidence when it comes to demanding the ball and trying to influence a game.

Kulusevski's directness and willingness to drive forward can give Spurs momentum when matches become scrappy.

Maddison, meanwhile, has the technical quality and self-belief to take responsibility in possession rather than hide when the stakes rise.

The midfield pair have also both returned from potential career-ending injuries and played a role in Spurs' 3-1 win over Coventry on Monday night.

Neither player can solve Tottenham's mentality problem alone; that responsibility must be shared across the dressing room.

But a team needs leaders who set standards in training, demand more from their teammates and refuse to accept a drop in intensity when a match becomes uncomfortable.

That is where De Zerbi's influence could prove important. A clear tactical identity can create confidence, while consistent expectations around work rate, concentration and accountability can help build trust between players.

Team spirit is not simply about celebrating together after a win. It is about tracking back for a teammate, responding positively after conceding and remaining united when the crowd grows anxious.

Tottenham have not had an unhappier away day destination in the Premier League era than Stamford Bridge.

Spurs have only beaten Chelsea once there, in 2018, since the 1990s and face their London rivals this weekend.

There have been embarrassing defeats, capitulations and the infamous Battle of the Bridge over recent years.

With Tottenham recording their first win of the season against Coventry last time out, De Zerbi's men will need to show huge character and collective resolve to get a result on Saturday.

The returns of Maddison and Kulusevski increase the quality of the Spurs team but also shows the individual resilience of the players in question.

The Spursy label will not disappear because of one good performance or result – but a spirited, competitive showing at Stamford Bridge would at least be the first step and show the fans the club is heading in the right direction.

articles.title: 'No messing about' - Eddie Howe backed to replace Michael Carrick as Manchester United manager
articles.summary: Former Bournemouth winger Marc Pugh has backed Eddie Howe to take over from under-fire head coach Michael Carrick at Manchester United. The 48-year-old tacti...
articles.body:
Former Bournemouth winger Marc Pugh has backed Eddie Howe to take over from under-fire head coach Michael Carrick at Manchester United. The 48-year-old tactician has emerged as a leading contender for the Old Trafford hotseat after Wednesday's humbling 4-1 Champions League defeat away at Como extended the club's winless run.

Former winger endorses managerial contender

Pugh believes his old boss possesses the ideal profile to revive the Red Devils should the hierarchy dismiss Carrick. Wednesday's loss in Italy stretched the club's winless streak to seven games across all competitions. According to talkSPORT , technical director Jason Wilcox favours appointing the 48-year-old if a change is made, though ex-Germany coach Julian Nagelsmann has also been sounded out .

Relentless intensity suits struggling squad

Signed by Howe in 2010, the 39-year-old former winger made 232 appearances under the Englishman during a nine-year stay at the Vitality Stadium that included promotions from both League One and the Championship.

Speaking on talkSPORT's Hawksbee and Baker show on Thursday, Pugh insisted the demanding coach would immediately raise standards behind the scenes: "If I was Eddie, I'd jump at the chance, but to be honest, I think United need someone like Eddie. The intensity level in training will go up a notch. He won't stand for people sacking training off.

"I'm not saying Michael does. I don't know what goes on behind the scenes at Old Trafford, at United, but he will make sure people that are playing on a Saturday and Tuesday, whenever it may be, that they are going to run and he plays high-press, high-intensity football.

"There will be no messing about, that's for sure, but he's fantastic tactically, technically, he cares about his players and I think they can do a lot worse than Eddie, that's for sure."

Silverware pedigree strengthens job credentials

Howe has been out of work since departing Newcastle United in July following a successful five-year tenure at St James' Park. During his time on Tyneside, he twice secured Champions League qualification and lifted the 2025 Carabao Cup to end the Magpies' 70-year wait for major domestic silverware, building on two memorable spells at Bournemouth either side of a nine-month stint with Burnley.

Having initially steered the Cherries out of League Two, he returned in 2012 to take them all the way to the Premier League. Asked whether his former manager would be tempted by the vacancy in Manchester, Pugh added: "I think jobs like that don't come around often and it's one of the best clubs in the world. You've got to jump at the chance in my eyes."

Despite the growing speculation surrounding his position, Carrick is set to remain in the dugout when United host Howe's former club Bournemouth on Sunday. Victory at Old Trafford is vital for the beleaguered head coach as he attempts to halt a seven-game slide and ease the scrutiny from the boardroom. However, another setback against the Cherries could prompt Wilcox and the club's decision-makers to accelerate their pursuit of a replacement.
