articles.title: Nick Woltemade makes history as he becomes only the third player to do this for Juventus
articles.summary: Nick Woltemade has now made history with Juventus. The Newcastle United loan striker joining Darko Kovačević and Roberto Baggio.
articles.body:
Nick Woltemade has now made history with Juventus.

The Newcastle United loan striker joining Darko Kovačević and Roberto Baggio.

Juventus now with three players to score in each of their first three major European appearances.

Nick Woltemade achieving this in the Europa League against NEC, Celta Vigo and now Rennes.

Juventus went ahead through Zeki Çelik after five minutes, Nick Woltemade with the assist.

Mousa Al-Taamari equalised and Boulaye Dia put Rennes ahead before half-time.

Up stepped Nick Woltemade though to level with a very coolly taken second-half penalty under huge pressure in front of the Juve fans.

The Newcastle United loan star was man of the match for Juventus and as well as his goal and assist, Big Nick linking up play so well as the Italian side created a host of chances. Very unlucky not to win the game as Jhon Lucumí's late winner was ruled out for offside by VAR.

Nick Woltemade spoke to Sky Sport Italia after the match: *"It's definitely very bitter [not to win], given how much we produced in the second half,. We deserved to win. It didn't happen and now we have to recover and think about Lecce. I politely asked Kolo Muani if I could take the penalty and he told me to go ahead. It went well and I scored. At the end I would have liked to get a third. The most important thing is to play a good game. Tonight we played with the right spirit and we'll carry on like that."*

Great to see Nick Woltemade in such excellent European form, three goals and an assist from three Europa League starts.

Also very refreshing to hear Big Nick having the confidence to want to take that high pressure penalty, wanting to take the responsibility.

It has all been ridiculously over the top since his loan move (only last month!) as the Italian media have made the Newcastle United loan player a scapegoat for Juventus' average start to the season, eighth in the table and only nine goals scored by Juve in seven league matches.

This Nick Woltemade criticism (blindly parroted by the UK media) especially ludicrous considering Big Nick hasn't yet had a chance to start a Serie A match, only 125 minutes in sub appearances.

Big Nick the big target for blame and yet never having even started a league game yet, whilst as stated above, in all three Europa League matches when getting the chance to start he has scored, plus a vital assist as well last night.

Following the game, Nick Woltemade made man of the match for Juventus with the highest rating of 8/10 from Goal going to the Newcastle United loan star: 'The undisputed protagonist for Juventus. He provided the assist for Celik's opener just six minutes in and remained the focal point of the attack throughout. Under immense pressure, he converted the 67th-minute penalty to secure the draw for his side.'

Not such a great night for former Newcastle United defender Lloyd Kelly rated 5/10: 'Utilised on the left of the defensive trio, Kelly provided some decent ball progression but was caught out of position during the build-up to Rennes' first goal. He was substituted in the 80th minute as Juve moved to a more aggressive shape.'

articles.title: Infantino re-election hopes boosted by Asia support
articles.summary: Gianni Infantino's hopes of being re-elected Fifa president are enhanced by an endorsement from the Asian Football Confederation.
articles.body:
Gianni Infantino's hopes of being re-elected Fifa president have been given a major boost by an endorsement from the head of the Asian Football Confederation.

President Sheikh Salman bin Ibrahim Al Khalifa Salman told the confederation's Congress in Tokyo - which was attended by Infantino - that "we reaffirm our full commitment, of course, to supporting you as you seek a new mandate as president".

Sheikh Salman's support represents a significant u-turn just two months after he signed a joint letter with the heads of Uefa and Concacaf criticising Infantino over his failed plan to sell stakes in the World Cup to private investors.

At the time the three confederations accused him of breaking trust "through deception" over the Fifa Forward Enterprise scheme.

But Sheikh Salman told the meeting in Japan it was time "to move forward".

"I've spoken to a lot of members within this continent. I know your feeling and I think your commitment is clear as well. Your support to Gianni is very clear," he added.

"So that's why Gianni I want to make it clear: yes, we had some issues, we spoke about them in the past, but let's not relate the two things together.

"The last few days we met in Zurich, you made it clear there was a clear understanding between us and that's why we're happy to have you here as well - we need to move forward.

"As one Asian family, we are ready to move forward, united in your support, Gianni, I just want to make that clear."

Alongside Infantino's power base in Africa and South America, Sheikh Salman's endorsement could be crucial in ensuring the Fifa president secures a fourth and final term.

At the election in Rabat in March, Uefa will have 55 votes, Africa 54, Asia 46, Concacaf 35, Oceania 11 and Conmebol 10.

The deadline for candidates to confirm they are standing against Infantino is 18 November - although none have yet filed and he could stand unopposed.

At a meeting of Fifa's Council last week, Infantino apologised for his World Cup sell-off plan , but failed to offer a full explanation for how the proposal was devised.

He also proposed to increase the amount of money handed out for football development across the world by $3.4bn (£2.6bn).

Uefa has since told Fifa it must release key documents and answer all questions relating to its governance and decision-making by 2 November.

articles.title: EFL preview: 'Sleepless nights' for under pressure bosses at Norwich City, Sheffield Wednesday and Bristol Rovers
articles.summary: Norwich City head coach Philippe Clement, Sheffield Wednesday manager Henrik Pedersen and Bristol Rovers boss Steve Evans face scrutiny.
articles.body:
As the daylight hours get shorter, perhaps so too does the amount of time left in the dugout for some EFL managers.

While never a pleasant topic of discussion, especially with the season only two months young, the ruthless nature of football means pressure is already mounting.

Over the past 48 hours, Crawley Town's Colin Kazim-Richards and Bromley boss Andy Woodman - the third longest-serving manager in the 92 - have exited their clubs.

There are, of course, plenty of teams flying high as we enter the final round of fixtures before the clocks go back.

Who might be hoping they can turn back time by the end of the weekend? Here are some key talking points to look out for in the EFL.

The first quarter of the campaign was not meant to be like this for Norwich City.

After Philippe Clement took over at Carrow Road last November , only four teams picked up more points in the Championship than the Canaries (56) through the remainder of the 2025-26 season.

Their strong form under the Belgian meant Norwich recovered from bottom of the table to finish ninth. Fans understandably had high hopes heading into 2026-27.

But it has started in similarly poor fashion to the last, with a run of five straight league defeats leaving Norwich in 21st on nine points from 11 games.

That is just one point and one place better off than they were at this stage last season under Liam Manning, who was sacked following another four consecutive losses.

"I've got egg on my face because they were my wild promotion pick so I'm as surprised as anyone that they're doing so badly," said former Hull City striker Aaron McLean.

"I thought the job Clement did when he came in last year was incredible and I really fancied them to kick on this season and not only challenge for the play-offs, but challenge for automatic promotion and be right up there.

"They've just been so disappointing and they look void of any confidence at the moment. I don't know where they go from here."

Norwich did suffer a major blow by losing striker Mohamed Toure , who had scored five goals in seven league games, to a shoulder injury which will keep him out for several months.

"It's my task to stay calm in the frustration because if everybody starts to panic, we are not going to have the season we want," Clement told BBC Radio Norfolk.

The next of those for the Canaries is against another side struggling for wins of late as they visit Charlton Athletic on Saturday (12:30 BST).

The Addicks have gone eight matches without victory since winning their opening three (D5 L3), though they are unbeaten at The Valley and have conceded just twice on home soil.

A win and a draw from their past two Championship games might not look like a big deal on paper for Cardiff City.

But when you factor in that the victory was a whopping 5-1 thrashing of Watford and the draw was at promotion favourites Middlesbrough , then there are signs of real hope for the Bluebirds.

Brian Barry-Murphy's side have won two of their past four league encounters - their only two wins of the campaign so far - to move up to 19th and three points clear of danger.

Cardiff can earn points and praise - Barry-Murphy

Cardiff will hope to back it up on Saturday with another positive result but they face a very tough test, with in-form Birmingham City the visitors to the Welsh capital (15:00 BST).

Blues have won three in a row and are unbeaten in five (W4 D1) - a run which has helped them rise to fourth in the table, two points off the automatic promotion spots.

Not to mention that Birmingham boss Chris Davies is a former Swansea City coach, so there might be some added spice to this one.

Third time lucky for high-flying Stockport?

When Dave Challinor walked out the door after almost five years in charge at Edgeley Park, there were some who did not expect Stockport to challenge for promotion again this season.

County have finished third but missed out on going up via the play-offs in the past two seasons - both of which were under Challinor.

But new boss Jimmy McNulty is working his magic for the Hatters, who are now top of League One after four wins in a row , climbing from ninth in the table five weeks ago.

Leading the way for Stockport is in-form striker Kyle Wootton. The 29-year-old has scored nine goals in 11 games and has netted in his past four.

County will be hoping this season is third time lucky for their ambition to win promotion to the second tier for the first time since 2002, following a journey down to National League North and back.

Their next test on Saturday is a trip to 18th-placed Notts County (15:00 BST), who ended a four-game losing run with a 2-0 victory over Sheffield Wednesday in midweek.

South Yorkshire derby for stuttering Owls

Early-season positivity after a long-awaited ownership takeover has now started to turn to frustration among some in the stands.

The Owls have dropped from top to seventh in League One after one win from their past five games (D3 L1).

Supporters have been less than convinced with performances and some were even calling for manager Henrik Pedersen to go during Tuesday's 2-0 defeat by the newly-promoted Magpies.

'Wednesday can't keep playing this poorly'

Pressure grows on Pedersen as Owls misfire

"You might look at the table and say this is harsh," said BBC Radio Sheffield's Rob Staton.

"No, this is just life at Sheffield Wednesday in League One. Just as it was in the past for other Owls managers, or anyone else managing a club of this size in the third tier.

"The odd bad result isn't a surprise when you have to rebuild the whole squad in a summer. But Wednesday simply can't keep playing as poorly as they are."

Up next is a trip to South Yorkshire rivals Doncaster Rovers (15:00 BST), who are 19th and only above the drop zone on goal difference.

Struggling Rovers host Swindon in M4 derby

All the talk before a ball was kicked was that Bristol Rovers would be right up there challenging for automatic promotion in League Two.

That looked like it would be the case when the Gas reeled off four wins in their opening five games.

At that stage, manager Steve Evans - who took over in December 2025 and saved the club from relegation last season - was on a run of 15 wins from 19 league matches in charge of Rovers.

But they have since plunged down the table to 16th after just one victory in seven, including four straight defeats.

"It's causing a lot sleepless nights," Evans told BBC Radio Bristol - and said he has been having phone conversations with his assistant Paul Raynor at 3am.

"[But] let's not get carried away with stats. We will bounce back for sure," he added.

Rovers will hope they can do just that when they host Swindon Town, managed by Gas legend Ian Holloway, in a West Country derby on Saturday.

The Robins are tied on 15 points with Rovers and one place above their rivals on goal difference only and on Tuesday ended an eight-match winless run, in all competitions, by winning 3-1 at second-placed Barnet - a result nobody saw coming.

BBC Sport will have live text coverage of all the weekend's EFL action, starting with Bolton v Middlesbrough (20:00 BST) on Friday and throughout Saturday's fixtures across the Championship, League One and League Two.

articles.standfirst: El Rayo reintegrará los tres partidos de Butarque y anuncia la vuelta de la Franja
articles.summary: El Rayo reintegrará los tres partidos de Butarque y anuncia la vuelta de la Franja
articles.body: El Rayismo llevaba mucho tiempo esperando y el club se ha movido. Después de una reunión interna, tal y cómo confirmó Beñat San José en la previa del encuentro ante el Elche, el Rayo Vallecano ha anunciado medidas. El club franjirrojo ha anunciado por un comunicado oficial que se compromete a "compensar a los abonados que, por causas total y absolutamente ajenas a ellos no hicieron uso de su abono, con la devolución de la parte proporcional correspondiente" de los tres encuentros que se disputaron en Butarque y anuncia la vuelta de la Franja para la temporada 27/28. El reintegro de la parte proporcional de los abonos por los tres partidos en Butarque es una de las peticiones que lleva exigiendo desde hace tiempo la afición. La Agrupación de Peñas del Rayo Vallecano anunció una serie de peticiones con la finalidad de "rebajar la tensión" de cara al encuentro ante el Elche y esta era la primera. "Esta compensación se producirá antes del 31 de diciembre de 2026. En los próximos días comunicaremos de qué forma se llevará a cabo", reza el comunicado oficial del club. Este anuncio del Rayo " se produce en un marco de comprensión de la situación, escucha activa de la afición y como gesto de acercamiento entre las partes", recalca el escrito. "Rayo Vallecano de Madrid lamenta profundamente el perjuicio que ha sufrido nuestra afición, y nuestro Club por el cierre total y absolutamente injustificado de nuestro estadio, que nos ha llevado a disputar tres partidos en el Estadio Municipal Ontime Butarque y se reserva las actuaciones que considere necesarias contra los culpables de dicha actuación. Tras una profunda reflexión, el Club entiende el dolor de nuestra afición por haber tenido que ver como su equipo jugaba de local en un estadio que no es el Estadio de Vallecas, su estadio. Lamentamos profunda y sinceramente el perjuicio que, por el cierre total y absolutamente injustificado que nos fue impuesto, ha sufrido la afición y el propio Club en los partidos que nos enfrentaron a Alavés, Real Racing Club de Santander y RCD Espanyol de Barcelona. Por todo ello, y pese a haber cumplido con las condiciones legales especificadas en el abono, el Club ha decidido compensar a los abonados que, por causas total y absolutamente ajenas a ellos no hicieron uso de su abono, con la devolución de la parte proporcional correspondiente a dichos encuentros. Esta compensación se producirá antes del 31 de diciembre de 2026. En los próximos días comunicaremos de qué forma se llevará a cabo. Esta actuación se produce en un marco de comprensión de la situación, escucha activa de la afición y como gesto de acercamiento entre las partes. Es la respuesta a la situación absolutamente injusta que se ha producido hacia nuestro club. Además, estamos en condiciones de anunciar que las equipaciones de la próxima temporada, 27/28 contarán con la franja como protagonista. Estas dos actuaciones suponen un paso adelante por parte del Club con la firme intención de lograr una normalidad que permita al equipo competir en las mejores condiciones posibles con el apoyo incondicional de su afición. articles.title: AC Milan renew interest in Real Madrid forward but receive clear response from the club – report
articles.summary: Real Madrid and Endrick have rejected an approach from AC Milan over a potential move for the Brazilian forward, according to Bernabeu Digital. As per the ou...
articles.body:
Real Madrid and Endrick have rejected an approach from AC Milan over a potential move for the Brazilian forward, according to Bernabeu Digital .

As per the outlet, the Italian club renewed its interest in the youngster around a month ago, but neither the player nor the Spanish giants is currently willing to consider a transfer.

Milan have continued to monitor Endrick's situation in Madrid, hoping to explore the possibility of bringing him to Serie A.

Their latest inquiry, though, has not changed the player's position or the club's plans.

Milan renew interest but Real Madrid refuse to entertain a move

Endrick has attracted interest from Milan before , although Real Madrid have been clear that they have no intention of letting the forward leave, while the Brazilian also remains determined to establish himself in Spain.

AC Milan have renewed their interest in Endrick. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images)

Notably, the renewed inquiry did not develop into negotiations because neither side was prepared to move forward.

Rather, Milan's interest should be viewed as an attempt to assess the situation rather than evidence that a transfer is close.

Endrick determined to succeed at Real Madrid

The Brazilian faces significant competition for attacking places at Real Madrid, making regular minutes difficult to secure.

Breaking into the first team requires him to compete with established players while adapting to the demands and expectations of one of Europe's biggest clubs.

Endrick does not want to leave Real Madrid. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images)

Despite that challenge, Endrick believes his future remains at the Bernabeu .

He is not convinced that moving to Italian football would be the right decision at this stage of his career, and Real Madrid also view him as a player with considerable room for development.

That position matters because a lack of playing time does not automatically mean a player wants to leave.

Endrick's immediate priority is to earn more opportunities within the existing setup rather than pursue a fresh start elsewhere.

articles.summary: Good morning and happy Friday. Yesterday brought the European and South American international action to a close. Here are the day's top 5 stories to keep yo...
articles.body:
Good morning and happy Friday. Yesterday brought the European and South American international action to a close. Here are the day's top 5 stories to keep you up to date with the football world.

The build-up to El Clásico is heating up

Real Madrid face a crucial LaLiga clash this Sunday when they visit Spotify Camp Nou. Los Blancos head into the big game in peak form after rounding off a perfect week in European competition.

The mood in the opposing camp is very different following their European setback. FC Barcelona go into the clash with defensive concerns after suffering a heavy 4-2 defeat away to Paris Saint-Germain.

Barça have won every home game since November 2025; Real Madrid, coming off four straight wins, are looking to end their rivals' home dominance.

Real Sociedad and Celta win in the Europa League

Last night was a glorious one for the Spanish sides in the Europa League. Both teams secured their first wins in international competition and are dreaming of going further in the tournament.

Matarazzo's side showed their quality by thrashing Norway's Lillestrom 6-0 away, putting the game to bed in the first half thanks to a hat-trick of assists from Mikel Oyarzabal and goals from Sergio Gómez and Luka Sucic.

Celta secured a valuable European victory after coming from behind to beat Celtic 2-1 away in Glasgow. Although the Scottish side took the lead through Mika Baur early in the second half, a brilliant brace from Javi Rodríguez turned the game around and sealed the first continental win for Claudio Giráldez's team.

Estudiantes beat Flamengo to reach the Copa Libertadores final

Estudiantes de La Plata beat the Brazilian side in a penalty shootout (2-3) and will play in the final on November 28 at the Estadio Centenario in Montevideo.

After holding out for more than 40 minutes with ten men following Baltasar Rodríguez's sending-off in a tense 0-0 draw, Fernando Muslera stood tall in the shootout, saving three crucial penalties from Jorginho, Lucas Paquetá and Bruno Henrique.

European surprises: Milan and Juve stumble; Benfica and Leverkusen deliver

Elsewhere in Europe, the heavy defeats of continental giants stood out, with AC Milan thrashed 3-0 by Bournemouth and Olympique Lyonnais also suffering a resounding 3-0 loss to Hoffenheim.

Meanwhile, Juventus could only draw 2-2 at home to Rennes and Beşiktaş drew 2-2 with Crystal Palace, while Bayer Leverkusen, who won 2-0 at OFI Crete, and Benfica, who thrashed Omonia Nicosia 4-1 away, were among the night's success stories.

José Bordalás exploded in his press conference following Getafe's heavy 5-2 defeat to Lugano in the Conference League, launching a scathing attack on the club's board.

"The promises made to me haven't been kept. I feel deceived. As a coach, I don't deserve this," the Alicante-born manager said firmly, visibly furious with the squad planning. Pulling no punches, he declared that the squad "isn't even good enough for one competition" and warned that rotation was over: from now on, only his first-choice players would play, even at the risk of injury.

articles.title: El aviso del capitán del Deportivo antes de enfrentarse al Atlético
articles.standfirst: Diego Villares analizó en La Tribu el duelo su equipo y el de Simeone, la exigencia de Primera División y sus sensaciones ante el Real Madrid-Barcelona
articles.summary: Diego Villares analizó en La Tribu el duelo su equipo y el de Simeone, la exigencia de Primera División y sus sensaciones ante el Real Madrid-Barcelona
articles.body: Diego Villares tiene una cosa clara de cara al primer Clásico de la temporada: el Barcelona llega en mejor momento que el Real Madrid. El capitán del Deportivo de La Coruña se pasó por los micrófonos de La Tribu, donde conversó con Raúl Varela antes del encuentro de su equipo ante el Atlético de Madrid, y también dio su pronóstico para el duelo entre los dos grandes del fútbol español. "Personalmente creo que ahora está más fuerte el Barça", reconoció Villares. No obstante, el futbolista gallego advirtió de que un partido de estas características siempre está abierto: "En ese tipo de partidos, al final, cualquier cosa con la calidad de los jugadores que tienen esos equipos y los presupuestos que manejan, al final cualquier jugador decide un partido y creo que puede marcarse en los pequeños detalles". El capitán deportivista también repasó el regreso del conjunto gallego al fútbol profesional y la exigencia que está encontrando en la máxima categoría. Villares destacó el nivel de los rivales y la importancia de evitar errores que puedan resultar decisivos. "Era algo que ya nos podríamos esperar, sobre todo el nivel de todos los equipos, toda la calidad que hay en todas las plantillas", explicó. El jugador considera que la igualdad de la competición convierte cada jornada en un desafío. "Ahora con nada, cualquier equipo te crea una ocasión en clara, te hace gol y eso al final se nota", señaló al analizar cómo los pequeños detalles pueden cambiar el desarrollo de los encuentros. Sobre los objetivos del Deportivo, Villares fue prudente y puso la permanencia como primera meta. "En un principio por lo menos hacer esos 43 puntos que son necesarios cuanto antes", afirmó. El Deportivo afronta una visita exigente al Atlético de Madrid. Villares reconoció el potencial de la plantilla rojiblanca y destacó los recursos de los que dispone Diego Simeone, incluso después de disputar un partido europeo entre semana. "Sabemos el nivel de la plantilla del Atlético de Madrid, aunque hayan jugado entre semana, el fondo de armario que tienen y los jugadores que tiene a su disposición Simeone yo creo que es una pasada", comentó. Pese a las dificultades, el capitán blanquiazul dejó claro que el Dépor no renuncia a competir ante ningún rival. "Lo más bonito es competir fin de semana tras fin de semana contra cualquier rival e intentar hacerle daño con tus armas y sacarle el máximo rédito posible".
